PullRequest.Title: Fix permission bits in mock-policy-server file commands
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses the permission bit settings for file-based configurations in the mock-policy-server to ensure compliance with SDK/runtime requirements. 

Changes made include:

- Updated macOS and Linux commands to explicitly set `root` ownership and mode `0644`, ensuring files are root-owned and not group/world-writable, even when overwriting existing files.
- No changes were made to Windows commands, as the runtime does not enforce equivalent ACL checks.
- Revised the README.md to reflect these updates.
- Applied consistent fixes to both UI-generated commands in `app.ts` and the control API in `server.ts`.

Validation has been completed successfully, confirming that the changes meet the necessary requirements.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editing the Managed Settings JSON in the browser UI and rendering per-platform deployment commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor input synchronously parses and pretty-prints the current JSON, builds three command strings, and assigns them to existing code elements. The diff only lengthens the macOS and Linux string templates by a constant amount; no subprocess, filesystem, IPC, database, or network operation runs on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One render per editor input, with string work scaling with the single current JSON body; two Unix command templates receive only constant additional text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser event-loop execution per input event; debounced server persistence is separate and unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used for deployment command strings; they are regenerated on each relevant render before and after the diff. The changed constant suffix does not alter cache behavior or effective cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call sites show renderFileDeploy runs on editor input and the changed helpers only return template strings.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Managed-settings bodies can vary in size, but the body was already embedded into and assigned through the same three command strings before the diff. The added text is constant-size and does not change asymptotic CPU, allocation, or DOM-write cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The hot UI path gains only constant-size string content and no new expensive boundary, retained state, fan-out, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fetching GET /api/file-deployment from the mock policy server
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request synchronously reads the in-memory managedSettings body, JSON-stringifies it once, constructs one response object, and serializes it to the HTTP response. The diff changes only constant command-template text.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return the generated deployment metadata as one HTTP JSON response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One response per explicit GET request, containing one grouped payload for all three platforms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The endpoint already generated and returned the same grouped platform payload over one HTTP response; only two command string values were shorter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response serialization and socket write must complete for the caller, but payload growth from this diff is constant and small.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with explicit API request count and the single current settings body, not with endpoints, files, or platforms beyond the fixed set of three.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One independent synchronous construction per incoming request; no added queue, limiter, subprocess, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No endpoint cache or coalescing exists before or after the diff; state is read from memory on each explicit request. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent for the changed command construction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the route directly calls getFileDeployment, whose changed lines perform no I/O or subprocess execution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request frequency is not established, but even repeated requests add only a fixed number of bytes and fixed template concatenation work per response.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. There is no added network call, boundary fan-out, or input-dependent amplification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copying and explicitly executing a generated macOS or Linux file-install command on a client machine
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the user copies and runs one command, the shell creates the destination directory if needed, writes one managed-settings.json file, then sets owner and mode before completion. The new chown and chmod are on this explicit install command's critical path and enforce the intended file metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch sudo sh and execute cat, chown, and chmod for one destination file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell command per explicit user deployment; exactly one destination file and two newly added metadata operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command used sudo tee to write the same single file and did not explicitly run chown or chmod.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The metadata operations must complete before the install command succeeds, but they are fixed-cardinality local operations on the file just written.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write managed-settings.json, change its owner to root, and set mode 0644.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file write plus one ownership change and one mode change per explicit install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file was written once via tee; ownership and mode were inherited/preserved rather than explicitly updated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All operations are serial and complete before the command returns; none scale with policy count or directory contents.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales only with the number of explicit deployment executions, not JSON size for the metadata operations and not a collection size; effective per-run cardinality is one file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations are serialized by && within one explicit shell invocation: mkdir, file write, chown, then chmod. There is no burst or per-item concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates. A repeated deployment repeats the same fixed operations on one file both before and after the diff; there is no retained key set or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the generated shell sequence directly shows the added serial chown/chmod operations and the README states the server does not execute them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact process startup and local filesystem latency vary by OS, but cardinality is fixed at one file and deployment is an explicit, infrequent administrative action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added fixed local metadata operations are necessary to establish required permissions and occur only during an explicit one-file deployment, with no realistic hot-path or scaling impact.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced UI rendering, control-API generation, and execution of copied Unix deployment commands. The diff adds constant-size string content and two fixed local metadata operations to an explicit one-file install; it introduces no hot-path scaling, fan-out, retention, cache-lifecycle issue, or meaningful latency regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
